document_sha256_verified: yes -- verified by the seat against the pin before review
central_claim_as_understood: The NR4A3 5' fusion partner is a CANDIDATE, not established, stratification variable in EMC. Two separable questions are in different states: (a) prognosis now has a crude pooled magnitude (disease-specific death 7/15 = 46.7% TAF15 vs 6/58 = 10.3% EWSR1 over 73 patients from two non-overlapping cohorts) that arrives with a published defeater; (b) treatment response has direction only (0 of 3-5 TAF15 patients) and can have no magnitude, because a zero-event arm yields none at any denominator. Prevalence pooling puts TAF15 at 18.2% (12.9-25.0) of partner-assigned EMC, an interval that CONTAINS rather than corrects the literature's ~20%.

blockers.where: Abstract (line 78): 'Local recurrence (26.7 % vs 22.4 %) and distant metastasis (33.3 % vs 24.1 %) show no material separation.' Echoed in S3.3 as 'What survives is the negative, and it is stronger than the reversal was.'
blockers.what: An absence-of-effect claim the data cannot carry. Recomputed Newcombe 95% CIs on the risk difference (TAF15 minus EWSR1): local recurrence +4.3 pts (-15.7 to +31.0); distant metastasis +9.2 pts (-12.8 to +35.8). A 31-to-36-point TAF15 excess is fully compatible with both rows. The paper's own artifact contradicts the abstract: cohorts[agaram-2014-outcome].follow_up_warning states that on exactly these two rows informative censoring by the competing event biases the arm with more deaths DOWNWARD, so 'the two-cohort null is not evidence that those endpoints do NOT differ by partner, only that this record cannot establish that they do.' And S3.3 itself says the 4.3-point local-recurrence figure 'is a cancellation of two cohorts that disagree, not a small effect they share' (comparator arms 6.2% vs 28.6%, chi2 p=0.068) - the abstract states as a finding of no separation the very number the body calls a cancellation artifact.
blockers.why_blocking: It converts 'not established, in either direction' (which the body states correctly and the evidence supports) into 'no separation' at the one place most readers stop. Correction register A32 recorded this exact repair on 2026-08-27 and concluded 'no number moves and no manuscript sentence was wrong' after inspecting S3.3's follow-up sentence only; the abstract sentence and S3.3's 'what survives is the negative' were never checked, so the round-9 repair is INCOMPLETE in the manuscript. Fix: replace 'show no material separation' with the body's own form ('are not established by either cohort, in either direction') and print the risk-difference intervals.

blockers.where: S6 falsifier #5 and its twin in the artifact's what_could_kill_this[4] / zero_death_patients_to_reconcile()
blockers.what: The 'both choices make this falsifier easier to trigger' sentence is a completeness claim about the conservatism accounting and it is false. A third, undeclared degree of freedom dominates the answer: the TAF15 arm is summarised by a POINT ESTIMATE while every other contrast in this paper is judged by its Wilson interval. Recomputed with the TAF15 event count and the whole comparator arm held fixed exactly as the generator does: paper's criterion (TAF point estimate <= comparator Wilson upper 20.8%) k=19; TAF point <= comparator point k=53; INTERVAL OVERLAP (TAF Wilson lower <= comparator Wilson upper) k=3; post-hoc Fisher p >= 0.05 k=10. So one third cohort of 7 zero-death TAF15 patients gives 7/22 = 31.8% (95% CI 16.4-52.7) against 4.8-20.8 - the intervals now overlap - and drives Fisher p from 0.0034 to 0.0373; a cohort of 10 takes it to p = 0.054.
blockers.why_blocking: Under the two summary statistics this paper actually prints for every contrast, one third cohort DOES overturn the death contrast, and S3.3/S5 use overlapping intervals as the marker of non-establishment for the metastasis row. Applying non-overlap as a standard that must not be undone by overlap is a double standard inside one document, and the sentence tells the reader the accounting is complete when the choice that matters most is unstated. Fix: state the third choice and print k under each criterion, or drop the 'both choices' sentence.

blockers.where: S2.5, 'Hazard ratios, survival models, Kaplan-Meier': 'No individual patient data exist for any cohort here, and the two cohorts that ran time-to-event analyses publish p-values without event counts.'
blockers.what: Wrong as committed, and contradicted three times by the same document. Huang 2023 ran a multivariable time-to-event analysis (S3.4 quotes HR 30.60 and HR 8.14; S4.7 calls them 'Huang 2023's own published values'; S1.3 calls it 'a pathology series with a survival analysis') AND publishes the per-partner event counts S3.3 pools. S1.2 counts four series testing the partner against outcome, of which at least three (Huang, Paioli, Suemitsu) ran survival analyses. So neither 'two' nor 'without event counts' holds.
blockers.why_blocking: A false statement of fact in the Methods section that justifies a methodological refusal. The binding justification (no IPD) survives, so the fix is one clause - but the sentence as pinned is not true, and no guard in research/manuscripts/tests/ binds it.

p1s.where: Abstract ('a 36.3-point gap'), S3.3 table 'gap' column, S5 ('the pooled gap is 9.2 points')
p1s.what: No interval is given for any risk difference anywhere in the paper or the artifact, although the risk difference IS the estimand every headline sentence claims. Each arm gets a Wilson interval; the contrast gets a bare point. Recomputed Newcombe 95% CIs: death +36.3 (12.1 to 60.2); local recurrence +4.3 (-15.7 to +31.0); distant metastasis +9.2 (-12.8 to +35.8). The death row's interval STRENGTHENS the paper and costs nothing; the other two are what make STAT-B-1 impossible to write.

p1s.where: Whole manuscript - the string 'competing risk' does not occur in the prose. Present in the artifact and in correction register A32.
p1s.what: Competing risks are never named in the prose, and two consequences go uncarried. (i) Disease-specific death pooled as a crude uncensored proportion treats death from other causes as a non-event; neither source reports other-cause deaths, so the DSS proportions are not comparable across arms with unequal observation. (ii) The artifact's signed statement - that death as a competing risk biases the TAF15 recurrence and metastasis rates DOWNWARD, so those nulls are not evidence those endpoints do NOT differ - appears in no manuscript sentence. THIS IS WHERE THE PAPER IS LESS CAREFUL THAN ITS OWN ARTIFACT, and it is the same place STAT-B-1 lands.

p1s.where: S3.1: 'The direction is consistent across two cohorts, two drugs and five years of accrual'
p1s.what: Asserts cross-cohort replication that the paper's own primary analysis exists to deny. The artifact records 'Worst case both TAF15 patients here are among the trial's three'; if so the TAF15 direction is one cohort of three patients, not two, and the accrual span belongs to the comparator arms rather than the TAF15 observation. The worst-case qualification appears three paragraphs later but not on the sentence making the replication claim.

The secondary pool's comparator arm is not exchangeable and the abstract drops the spread: sunitinib 6/8 = 75.0% vs pazopanib 4/19 = 21.1%, two different drugs, spread 53.9 pts, Fisher p = 0.0248. S3.1's table prints the per-cohort values; the abstract prints only the pooled 37.0%. The asymmetry of standard is the finding: S3.3 refuses to let a 22.4-point comparator spread at p = 0.068 stand as a pooled figure, while a 53.9-point spread at p = 0.025 gets no equivalent sentence anywhere.

p1s.where: S3.3 Fisher tests and S3.1 secondary; S2.5's list of methods deliberately not used
p1s.what: Every Fisher test is run on a table pooled ACROSS cohorts, i.e. with the study stratum collapsed. No stratified analogue (Mantel-Haenszel or exact conditional) is computed, and S2.5 - which explains at length why random effects, I-squared and time-to-event were refused - does not mention the choice. It happens not to distort the death row (per-cohort gaps 36.7 and 38.1 against a pooled 36.3), which is worth stating; on local recurrence the collapse is exactly what produces the cancellation S3.3 then has to explain in prose.

p2s.what: 'Where only one cohort contributes - the entire TKI-response analysis - the pool is a single-cohort Wilson interval.' Only the PRIMARY analysis is single-cohort; the secondary pools two cohorts (0/5 and 10/27) and carries its own heterogeneity block.

Two quantities that look like the same quantity and are not: the pooled EWSR1 outcome denominator (16 Agaram + 42 Huang = 58) numerically coincides with Huang's own cohort size (58). Both are printed; nothing warns the reader they are different populations.

The defeater's denominators are Huang's PARTNER-ASSIGNED counts (7/9 TAF15, 12/46 EWSR1) while the pooled outcome table uses the with-follow-up counts (8 and 42). S4.7 explains the 58->53->50 accounting but never states that the confounder analysis and the pooled contrast run on different denominators of the same cohort.

An OVERALL-survival null used beside a DISEASE-SPECIFIC-death pool. S4.7 explicitly warns that DFS/DMFS are 'a different estimand entirely'; no equivalent note attaches to the OS null. The artifact IS more careful here (context_note names the endpoint mismatch), a second instance of the artifact outrunning the prose.
'several sit exactly at zero events' - exactly two strata do (0/3 and 0/5), and they are the same stratum viewed under two analyses.
'The largest partner-stratified series anywhere in this synthesis has 67 patients' - Paioli's partner-ASSIGNED n is 62; 67 is the series size, and 62 is what the prevalence pool uses.

what_i_could_not_break: Every printed statistic reproduces exactly from the printed integers: 16 Wilson intervals and 6 Fisher exact two-sided p-values independently recomputed, zero discrepancies.

The reconciliation threshold is arithmetically correct under its stated criterion (k = 19, total denominator 34), and BOTH conservatism directions it declares are correctly signed - holding the comparator fixed does bring the threshold nearer, and using the Wilson upper bound rather than the point estimate takes k from 53 to 19. The blocker is only that the accounting is presented as complete when it is not.

The prevalence pool is defensible as a fixed-effect pool: across four series the TAF15 share is homogeneous (29.2/15.8/18.2/16.1 %, chi2 = 2.34, df = 3, p = 0.505, I-squared = 0%), so the Wilson interval on 28/154 is not falsely narrow. Independence argued on author lists, institutions and continents with no counterexample found.

S3.5's containment language is exactly right and is the sentence this class of paper usually gets wrong: 'This pooling therefore does not correct that figure: it replaces a point estimate with an interval.' The excluded abstracts genuinely bracket it and the excluded Sjogren series genuinely sits ABOVE it, reported against the paper's own interest.
Crude cohort-collapsed pooling creates no Simpson reversal on the death row: per-cohort gaps 36.7 and 38.1 points against a pooled 36.3.
The S3.3 follow-up paragraph correctly REFUSES to sign the bias on the death row and retracts an earlier version that signed it; the circularity argument is right and is the harder thing to say.

Zero-event handling is correct and consistently applied: Wilson rather than normal, 'a zero-event arm yields no magnitude at any denominator', and the refusal to describe 0/3-0/5 as predicting non-response.

The declared refusals in S2.5 (no DerSimonian-Laird, no I-squared, no hazard ratios) are correct calls at these stratum sizes, and S4.2's insistence that the pooled figures are weighted descriptive summaries rather than meta-analytic estimates is the right disclaimer.

The paper is MORE careful than its artifact in one place: S3.4 downgrades Paioli 2021 to 'adjustment structure UNKNOWN' and refuses to count it as a second multivariable result, and S3.3 marks the metastasis attribution as 'by record and not by quotation' - honest self-weakenings no artifact field forced.
